chunks.arabic_text: وَإِنَّ أَبْوَابَ السَّمَاءِ لَا تُغْلَقُ تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ لِأَصْوَاتِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ لَهُمْ دَوِيٌّ كَدَوِيِّ النَّحْلِ يَقُولُ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ

translations.en: Indeed, the gates of the heaven are not closed on that night to the voices of the believers; they have a humming like the humming of bees. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:

chunks.arabic_text: «أَنَا رَبُّكُمْ وَأَنْتُمْ عِبَادِي أَدَّيْتُمْ حَقِّي وَحَقٌّ عَلَيَّ أَنْ أَسْتَجِيبَ لَكُمْ»

translations.en: "I am your Lord, and you are My servants. You have fulfilled My right, and it is a duty upon Me to answer you."

chunks.arabic_text: فَيَحُطُّ تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ عَمَّنْ أَرَادَ أَنْ يُحَطَّ عَنْهُ ذُنُوبُهُ وَيَغْفِرُ لِمَنْ أَرَادَ أَنْ يُغْفَرَ لَهُ.

translations.en: So on that night, He removes from whomever He wills to have his sins removed, and He forgives whomever He wills to be forgiven.

en.summary: This hadith describes the great virtue of that night, when the supplications of the believers rise unhindered and are received by Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It emphasizes divine mercy, the acceptance of du'a, and the removal and forgiveness of sins for those granted this grace.
en.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the acceptance of du'a and forgiveness on the night of 'Arafah?

key_terms.أَبْوَابَ السَّمَاءِ: the gates of heaven, symbolizing openness to mercy and response
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the believers whose voices and supplications are being described
key_terms.دَوِيٌّ: a humming or resonant sound, likening their voices to bees
key_terms.عِبَادِي: My servants, expressing the relationship between Allah and the worshippers
key_terms.حَقِّي: My right, referring to what the servants have fulfilled toward Allah
key_terms.أَسْتَجِيبَ: I answer or respond, referring to Allah's response to supplication
key_terms.ذُنُوبُهُ: his sins, which are removed from the one granted mercy
key_terms.يُغْفَرَ: to be forgiven, referring to divine pardon
